advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Classify transient object-read errors in _fold_heads' merge-tree/commit-tree failures the same way _publish_and_prune does, instead of always raising a heads-conflict with the fsck-recover hint.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/s3_doctor.py:277 `if merged.returncode != 0:` raises S3DoctorConflict tagged as a 'heads conflict'
src/rebar/_store/s3_doctor.py:294 `if commit.returncode != 0:` raises S3DoctorConflict with default fsck-recover hint
src/rebar/_store/s3_doctor.py:359 `if is_transient_object_read_error(create.stderr or create.stdout or "")` — _publish_and_prune explicitly separates transient object-read failures from conflicts
The _git seam docstring (lines 50-58) notes transient read faults are retried but can still survive ('three times on CI'), which is why the bundle path added the distinct hint.
advisory.finding: In _fold_heads, any non-zero exit from `merge-tree --write-tree` or `commit-tree` is unconditionally raised as S3DoctorConflict with the default 'run rebar fsck-recover' hint, even when the underlying failure is a transient object-read error rather than a genuine heads conflict. _publish_and_prune deliberately distinguishes this case (is_transient_object_read_error -> different hint), so the fold path attributes errors less precisely than the bundle path in the same module.
scenarios: A transient runner-FS object-read blip surviving the seam retries during merge-tree/commit-tree surfaces to the operator as a spurious 'tickets store heads conflict; run rebar fsck-recover'.

advisory.finding: The new unborn-branch path in _fold_heads (`if not tip: tip = rev-parse head_ref; continue`) is untested. Every seeding helper (_seed_two_divergent_bundles, _policy_tracker) clones with `-b tickets`, so refs/heads/tickets always resolves and the probe branch (returncode==0) is always taken. No test exercises a tracker whose published branch is unborn, where the first fetched head must BECOME the tip.
